tool.name: Fastplong
tool.command:
#import re
## Link input files
#set ext = '.fastq'
#if $in.is_of_type('fastq.gz') #set ext = '.fastq.gz' #end if
#set $in_name = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($in.element_identifier)) + $ext ln -sf '$in' '$in_name' &&
## Run fastplong fastplong
--thread "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --report_title 'fastplong report for $in_name' --in '$in_name' --out long${ext}
#if $ont_summary: --ont_summary '$ont_summary' #end if
#if $reads_to_process: --reads_to_process '$reads_to_process' #end if
## Adapter Trimming Options
#if $adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.disable_adapter_trimming == 'yes' --disable_adapter_trimming #else
#if str($adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.start_adapter): --start_adapter '$adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.start_adapter' #end if
#if str($adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.end_adapter): --end_adapter '$adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.end_adapter' #end if
#if $adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.adapter_fasta: --adapter_fasta '$adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.adapter_fasta' #end if
--distance_threshold $adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.distance_threshold --trimming_extension $adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.trimming_extension
## Chimeric read handling
#if str($adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.chimera.handling) == 'disable' --disable_chimera_splitting #else if str($adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.chimera.handling) == 'discard' --discard_chimeric_reads #else --chimera_min_segment_length $adapter_trimming_options.adapter_trim.chimera.chimera_min_segment_length #end if #end if
## Global Trimming Options
#if str($global_trimming_options.trim_front): --trim_front $global_trimming_options.trim_front #end if
#if str($global_trimming_options.trim_tail): --trim_tail $global_trimming_options.trim_tail #end if
## Filter Options
## Quality filtering options
#if $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.disable_quality_filtering == 'yes' --disable_quality_filtering #else
#if str($filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.qualified_quality_phred): --qualified_quality_phred $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.qualified_quality_phred #end if #if str($filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.unqualified_percent_limit): --unqualified_percent_limit $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.unqualified_percent_limit #end if #if str($filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.n_base_limit): --n_base_limit $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.n_base_limit #end if #if str($filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.n_percent_limit): --n_percent_limit $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.n_percent_limit #end if #if str($filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.mean_qual): --mean_qual $filter_options.quality_filtering_options.qual_filt.mean_qual #end if #end if
## Length filtering options
#if $filter_options.length_filtering_options.len_filt.disable_length_filtering == 'yes' --disable_length_filtering #else #if str($filter_options.length_filtering_options.len_filt.length_required): --length_required $filter_options.length_filtering_options.len_filt.length_required #end if
#if str($filter_options.length_filtering_options.len_filt.length_limit): --length_limit $filter_options.length_filtering_options.len_filt.length_limit #end if #end if
## GC content filtering options
#if str($filter_options.gc_filtering_options.min_gc): --min_gc $filter_options.gc_filtering_options.min_gc #end if #if str($filter_options.gc_filtering_options.max_gc): --max_gc $filter_options.gc_filtering_options.max_gc #end if
## Low complexity filtering options
#if $filter_options.low_complexity_filter.compl_filt.low_complexity_filter == 'yes' --low_complexity_filter
#if str($filter_options.low_complexity_filter.compl_filt.complexity_threshold): --complexity_threshold $filter_options.low_complexity_filter.compl_filt.complexity_threshold #end if #end if
## Read Modification Options
### PolyX tail trimming
#if $read_mod_options.polyx_tail_trimming.polyx.trim_poly_x == 'yes' --trim_poly_x #if $read_mod_options.polyx_tail_trimming.polyx.poly_x_min_len --poly_x_min_len $read_mod_options.polyx_tail_trimming.polyx.poly_x_min_len #end if #end if
### Per read cutting by quality options
#if $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.trim_side == 'front' --cut_front
#if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_window_size): --cut_front_window_size $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_window_size #end if #if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_mean_quality): --cut_front_mean_quality $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_mean_quality #end if
#else if $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.trim_side == 'tail' --cut_tail
#if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_window_size): --cut_tail_window_size $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_window_size #end if #if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_mean_quality): --cut_tail_mean_quality $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_mean_quality #end if
#else if $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.trim_side == 'both' --cut_front --cut_tail
#if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_window_size): --cut_front_window_size $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_window_size #end if #if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_mean_quality): --cut_front_mean_quality $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_front_mean_quality #end if #if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_window_size): --cut_tail_window_size $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_window_size #end if #if str($read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_mean_quality): --cut_tail_mean_quality $read_mod_options.cutting_by_quality_options.qual_trim.cut_tail_mean_quality #end if
#end if
### Low quality region handling (mask / break / best segment)
#if str($read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.mode) == 'mask' --mask --mask_window_size $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.mask_window_size --mask_mean_quality $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.mask_mean_quality
#else if str($read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.mode) == 'break' --break --break_window_size $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.break_window_size --break_mean_quality $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.break_mean_quality
#else if str($read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.mode) == 'best_segment' --best_read_segment --best_read_segment_window_size $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.best_read_segment_window_size --best_read_segment_mean_quality $read_mod_options.lowqual_region.lowqual_mode.best_read_segment_mean_quality
#end if
## Read sampling and selection options
#if str($sampling_options.select_mode.mode) == 'target_bases' --target_bases $sampling_options.select_mode.target_bases
#else if str($sampling_options.select_mode.mode) == 'sample_rate' --sample_rate $sampling_options.select_mode.sample_rate --seed $sampling_options.select_mode.seed
#else if str($sampling_options.select_mode.mode) == 'best_reads' --best_reads $sampling_options.select_mode.best_reads
#else if str($sampling_options.select_mode.mode) == 'best_bases' --best_bases $sampling_options.select_mode.best_bases
#end if
## Output Options
#if $ext == '.fastq.gz' --compression $output_options.compression #end if
#if str($output_options.failed_out): $output_options.failed_out failed_reads.fastq #end if
&& mv long${ext} '${out}'

param.label: Input Long Reads
param.help: Input FASTQ file with long reads

param.label: ONT sequencing summary
param.help: Optional sequencing_summary.txt from an Oxford Nanopore run. Adds run-level QC charts to the HTML and JSON reports

param.label: Number of reads to process
param.help: Limit the number of reads to process. Useful for quick QC or creating subsets.

param.label: Disable adapter trimming
param.help: Adapter trimming is enabled by default. If this option is specified, adapter trimming is disabled.

param.label: Adapter sequence for read start
param.help: The adapter sequence (uppercase only) at read start (5'). Leave blank to auto-detect.

param.label: Adapter sequence for read end
param.help: The adapter sequence (uppercase only) at read end (3'). Leave blank to auto-detect.

param.label: FASTA file with adapter sequences
param.help: Specify a FASTA file to trim the reads by all the sequences in this FASTA file.

param.label: Adapter Distance Threshold
param.help: Threshold of sequence-adapter-distance/adapter-length (0.0 ~ 1.0), Higher values increase adapter detection sensitivity. ([0.25])

param.label: Adapter trimming extension
param.help: When an adapter is detected, extend the trimming to make cleaner trimming, default 10 means trimming 10 bases more [10].

param.name: handling
param.label: Chimeric read handling
param.help: Reads carrying an internal adapter are the signature of a chimeric (concatemeric) ligation event. Since fastplong 0.7.0 these reads are split into separate segments by default.

param.label: Minimum chimera segment length
param.help: Minimum segment length retained after splitting on internal adapters. Shorter segments are dropped. Default is 20.

param.label: Trim front (5') of read
param.help: Trim this many bases from the start (5') of each read. Default: 0.

param.label: Trim tail (3') of read
param.help: Trim this many bases from the end (3') of each read. Default: 0.

param.label: Disable quality filtering
param.help: Quality filtering is enabled by default. If this option is specified, quality filtering is disabled.

param.label: Qualified quality phred
param.help: The quality value that a base is qualified. Default 15 means phred quality >=Q15 is qualified.

param.label: Unqualified percent limit
param.help: How many percent of bases are allowed to be unqualified (0~100). Default 40 means 40%.

param.label: N base limit
param.help: If a read's number of N bases is >n_base_limit, then this read is discarded (0~1000000). 0 means no N is allowed. Default 1000000 means no N limit.

param.label: N percent limit
param.help: If a read's percentage of N bases is >n_percent_limit, then this read is discarded (0~100). Default 10 means 10%.

param.label: Mean read quality
param.help: If a read's mean_qual quality score < mean_qual, then this read is discarded. Default 0 means no requirement.

param.label: Disable length filtering
param.help: Length filtering is enabled by default. If this option is specified, length filtering is disabled.

param.label: Length required
param.help: Reads shorter than this value will be discarded. Default is 20.

param.label: Maximum length
param.help: Reads longer than this value will be discarded. Default is 0 and means no limitation.

param.label: Minimum GC content (%)
param.help: The minimum GC content percentage allowed for each read (0~100), computed as (G + C) / read length * 100. Default 0 means no minimum GC requirement.

param.label: Maximum GC content (%)
param.help: The maximum GC content percentage allowed for each read (0~100), computed as (G + C) / read length * 100. Default 100 means no maximum GC requirement.

param.label: Enable low complexity filter
param.help: The complexity is defined as the percentage of bases that is different from its next base. Default is No

param.label: Complexity threshold (%)
param.help: Threshold for low complexity filter (0~100). Default is 30, which means 30% complexity is required.

param.label: PolyX tail trimming
param.help: Enable polyX trimming on 3' ends.

param.label: PolyX minimum length
param.help: The minimum length to detect polyX in the read tail. 10 by default.

section.name: cutting_by_quality_options
section.title: Per read cutting by quality options

param.name: trim_side
param.label: Activate trimming by quality
param.help: Enable per read trimming by quality on both sides/ front (5') only or tail (3') only, move a sliding window from over the read strating from the specified side, drop the bases in the window if its mean quality < threshold until window mean quality is above threshold

param.label: Front window size
param.help: Override window size for cut_front only. Default: cut_window_size

param.label: Front mean quality
param.help: Override quality threshold for cut_front only. Default: cut_mean_quality

param.label: Tail window size
param.help: Override window size for cut_tail only. Default: cut_window_size

param.label: Tail mean quality
param.help: Override quality threshold for cut_tail only. Default: cut_mean_quality

param.label: Front window size
param.help: Override window size for cut_front only. Default: cut_window_size

param.label: Front mean quality
param.help: Override quality threshold for cut_front only. Default: cut_mean_quality

param.label: Tail window size
param.help: Override window size for cut_tail only. Default: cut_window_size

param.label: Tail mean quality
param.help: Override quality threshold for cut_tail only. Default: cut_mean_quality

param.name: mode
param.label: Low quality region handling
param.help: Three alternative strategies for dealing with internal low quality regions, detected with a sliding window. They are mutually exclusive.
param.option: Mask low quality regions with N
Break reads, discarding the low quality regions
Keep only the best high quality segment of each read

param.label: Masking window size
param.help: The size of the sliding window used to evaluate the mean quality for N masking (5~1000000). Default is 50.

param.label: Masking mean quality
param.help: The mean quality requirement for the sliding window used for N masking (5~30). Default is 10 (Q10).

param.label: Breaking window size
param.help: The size of the sliding window used to evaluate the mean quality for read breaking (5~1000000). Default is 100.

param.label: Breaking mean quality
param.help: The mean quality requirement for the sliding window used for read breaking (5~30). Default is 10 (Q10).

param.label: Best segment window size
param.help: The size of the sliding window used by best-read-segment mode (5~1000000). Default is 100.

param.label: Best segment mean quality
param.help: The mean quality requirement for best-read-segment mode (5~30). Default is 10 (Q10).

param.name: mode
param.label: Sampling / selection mode
param.help: These modes are mutually exclusive and are applied after all filtering. Target bases, best reads and best bases all read the input twice.
param.option: No sampling - keep all reads passing the filters
Approximately target a number of output bases
Randomly keep a fraction of the reads
Keep the best N reads by mean quality
Keep the best reads up to N bases

param.label: Target bases
param.help: Approximately target this number of bases to output after filtering. The input is read twice.

param.label: Sample rate
param.help: Randomly keep this fraction of reads after filtering (0.0~1.0).

param.label: Random seed
param.help: Seed for reproducible output sampling. Default is 1.

param.label: Number of best reads
param.help: Keep the best N reads by mean quality after filtering. The input is read twice.

param.label: Best bases
param.help: Keep the best reads by mean quality until this many bases are selected after filtering. The input is read twice.

param.name: report_html
param.label: Output HTML report
param.help: Fastplong provides a QC report for the data before and after filtering within a single HTML page, which enables comparison of the quality statistics changed by the preprocessing step directly

param.name: report_json
param.label: Output JSON report
param.help: The JSON report contains all the data visualized in the HTML report. The format of the JSON report is manually optimized to be easily readable by humans and is compatible with MultiQC

param.label: Save failed reads?
param.help: Enable this to write failed reads to a separate FASTQ file.

param.label: Compression level
param.help: Compression level for gzip output (1~9). 1 is fastest, 9 is smallest. Only applied when the input, and therefore the output, is gzipped. Default is 4.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
fastplong_ is a tool designed to provide fast all-in-one preprocessing for long reads FASTQ files. This tool is developed in C++ with multithreading supported to afford high performance.
*Features*
1. Filter out bad reads (too low quality, too short, too many N, or outside a GC content range...)
2. Cut low quality bases for per read in its 5' and 3' by evaluating the mean quality from a sliding window (like Trimmomatic but faster)
3. Trim all reads in front and tail
4. Cut adapters. Adapter sequences can be automatically detected, which means you don't have to input the adapter sequences to trim them.
5. Detect chimeric (concatemeric) reads by their internal adapters and split them into separate segments, or discard them
6. Handle internal low quality regions by masking them with N, by breaking the read into pieces, or by keeping only the single best high quality segment
7. Trim polyX in 3' ends to remove unwanted polyX tailing (i.e. polyA tailing for mRNA-Seq data)
8. Subsample the output, either randomly or by keeping the highest quality reads
9. Report JSON format result for further interpreting
10. Visualize quality control and filtering results on a single HTML page (like FASTQC but faster and more informative)
11. Split the output to multiple files to support parallel processing (*Not enabled in this Galaxy tool*)
-----
**Chimeric reads**
An internal adapter in the middle of a long read is the signature of a chimeric read, produced when two or more molecules are ligated together. Since fastplong 0.7.0 such reads are **split into segments by default**, and segments shorter than the minimum segment length are dropped. Under **Adapter Trimming Options** you can instead choose to discard chimeric reads entirely, or to keep them intact.
-----
**Low quality regions**
Three mutually exclusive strategies are offered under **Read Modification Options**, all based on a sliding window:
* **Mask** replaces the bases of low quality regions with N, keeping the read length unchanged * **Break** discards the low quality regions, which may yield several fragments per input read * **Best segment** keeps only the single longest high quality stretch, so at most one fragment per input read
-----
**Sampling and selection**
Under **Read sampling and selection** the reads that pass all filters can be reduced further. The modes are mutually exclusive:
* **Target bases** approximately reaches a chosen number of output bases * **Sample rate** randomly keeps a fraction of the reads, reproducibly when a seed is given * **Best reads** / **Best bases** keep the highest mean quality reads, either a read count or a base budget
Target bases, best reads and best bases all read the input twice.
-----
**Inputs**
Single-end FASTQ or FASTQ.GZ long reads.
Optionally, a ``sequencing_summary.txt`` file from an Oxford Nanopore run can be supplied to add run-level QC charts to the reports.
-----
**Outputs**
* Processed reads
Optionally, under **Output Options** you can choose to output
* HTML report (default is Yes) * JSON report (compatible with MultiQC) * Failed reads (default is No)
**More Information**
- **Official Repository**: [GitHub - OpenGene/fastplong](https://github.com/OpenGene/fastplong)
.. _fastplong: https://github.com/OpenGene/fastplong
